column1: # b06 round 3: data names owned by save menu, text, input/Pak and cutscene modules

column3: SaveMenu_Update dispatches on the low state bits and uses upper bits for save/load and dialog transition flags.
SaveMenu_UpdateDialog indexes dialog layout and message tables with this value.
SaveMenu_UpdateDialog indexes five choice prompts and rectangles with this value.
Save, load and delete paths store Pak errors here; SaveMenu_RepairPak passes it to Pak_TryRepair.
Dialog input toggles this selection and SaveMenu_UpdateDialog uses it for cursor position.
Save-menu states assign frame delays and SaveMenu_UpdateDelay decrements this signed counter.
SaveMenu_UpdateSlotList changes it with navigation; load, save and delete use it to index slots.
SaveMenu_UpdateSlotList increments this modulo 16 to pace held-stick navigation.
The Pak error path increments it and tests it when deciding whether to retry or show an error.
Seventeen entries map displayed slots to Pak file numbers and extension bytes.
Sixteen save-header records are displayed in the slot list and written as the first Pak block.
SaveMenu_CaptureGameState copies game globals into this block; SaveMenu_RestoreGameState copies them back.
SaveMenu_RefreshFileList reads a Pak header here before copying it into a save-header slot.
SaveMenu_LoadSelectedFile reads the secondary Pak block here before copying it into game state.
Text_OpenWindow and Text_UpdateAndDrawWindows use this eight-entry table for per-character reveal timing.
Text_OpenWindow copies X, Y, width and height from the indexed rectangle.
Text_MeasureChoiceWindow updates this rectangle from choice rows; Text_OpenWindow copies it for choice windows.
Text_DrawTexturedRect copies this five-entry texture pointer table before selecting a texture.
Text_DrawTexturedRect copies these five tile width, height and mask records.
Text_OpenWindow increments it and Text_UpdateAndDrawWindows decrements it as windows close.
Text_UpdateAndDrawWindows copies the selected row here; NPC code tests whether it is zero.
Text_OpenWindow copies its row count and row pointers into a new choice window.
Four records hold per-window geometry, text, choices, cursor and animation state.
Text_LoadFontAssets clears it; Text_DrawEncodedString checks it before using font data.
Text_IsStickAdvanceHeld increments this counter until five strong-stick frames, then resets it.
Text_DrawEncodedString reads glyph width, height, advance and vertical offset from this table.
Text_DrawEncodedString emits this display list before drawing textured glyph rectangles.
Text_DrawEncodedString stores the current encoded glyph index here for metric lookup.
Text_DrawEncodedString adds this control-byte spacing to glyph advance.
Input_InitializeControllers picks the first usable controller port; gameplay and Pak code use it.
Input_ReadController copies the selected OSContPad stick_x here.
Input_ReadController copies the selected OSContPad stick_y here.
Input_ReadController stores the selected pad button bits here each frame.
Input_ReadController masks current buttons with the inverted previous mask to retain new presses.
Input_ReadController stores complement of current buttons here for next-frame edge detection.
Input_InitializeControllers creates this SI event queue and controller/Pak calls pass it as their message queue.
Four OSPfs structs initialized or repaired per controller port and used for file operations.
Pak_ScanGameFiles records matching file IDs, extension bytes, note count and free-space flags per port.
osContInit fills this bitmask and Input_InitializeControllers scans set bits for usable ports.
osContInit and osContGetQuery fill four OSContStatus records read for controller and Pak state.
OS_EVENT_SI sends this message through the controller SI queue.
Input_ReadController fills four OSContPad records via osContGetReadData.
Pak_ScanGameFiles compares this game-name byte field with Pak note names; allocation and deletion pass it to libultra.
Pak_AllocateGameFile copies this zero extension template before osPfsAllocateFile.
Pak_DeleteGameFile copies this zero extension template before osPfsDeleteFile.
Cutscene_ResetSequence zeros it; Cutscene_StartNextScene increments it and stops at 14 entries.
Cutscene_StartNextScene zeros it; Cutscene_UpdateScene increments it when sampling the camera track.
Cutscene_StartNextScene copies the camera track duration here and UpdateScene compares it to the current frame.
Cutscene_StartNextScene stores a pointer to the active camera track; UpdateScene samples it.
Cutscene_DrawImageCues increments this frame counter and compares it to cue start frames.
Cutscene_DrawImageCues advances this pointer when a cue's start frame is reached.
Thirty-two active image cue entries reset, allocated and drawn by Cutscene_DrawImageCues.
Text_DrawWindow and related text rendering load this palette before drawing glyph textures.
Menu texture drawing and number rendering load this 256-color palette.
SaveMenu_UpdateDialog indexes these five message pointers by choice prompt index.
SaveMenu_UpdateDialog indexes these five X/Y/width/height records for choice prompts.
SaveMenu_UpdateDialog selects messages from this contiguous table when menu bit 4 is set.
SaveMenu_UpdateDialog selects this 25-entry message table when menu bit 4 is clear.
SaveMenu_UpdateDialog indexes these 25 X/Y/width/height records by dialog index.
SaveMenu_UpdateDialog uses these four X/Y pairs to draw its two-choice cursor.
SaveMenu_UpdateSlotList chooses one of these pointers for a slot summary label.
Cutscene_DrawImageCues emits this display list before drawing cue rectangles.
Cutscene_StartEntry sets 60; Cutscene_UpdateMessageSequence decrements it between message windows.
Cutscene_StartEntry copies the entry's message count; UpdateMessageSequence decrements it per message.
Cutscene_StartEntry copies the entry message pointer here; Cutscene_UpdateMessageSequence reads one message/name pair and advances it.
